_comment: Observed peak CPU / RAM / wall clock per CI job, and the input to
check_runner_advice.py. Refresh with:
npm run check:ci-runner-advice -- --refresh --branch main
which harvests the `PROFILER_BASELINE_V1` rows the runner profiler writes
as `::notice` annotations (.ci/scripts/ci/profiler/panel.sh). The GATE
itself never touches the network: it compares these committed numbers
against the `runs-on:` in the workflow files, so `npm run ci` stays
offline-safe. This mirrors job-timeout-baseline.json deliberately, down to
the refresh/verify split and the stale-baseline check.
WHY AN ANNOTATION HARVEST AND NOT A STEP SUMMARY. The profiler's human
panel is a step summary, and a step summary cannot be read back through
the API at all -- there is no endpoint for it. Check-run ANNOTATIONS can,
which is the only reason a machine-readable row exists beside the panel.
WHY THE REFRESH IS MANUAL. A gate that rewrites its own baseline from CI
is a gate that ratifies whatever CI currently does: a job that crept onto
a bigger runner would be recorded as correct on the next run. Refreshing
is a commit somebody makes and a reviewer sees.
DELIBERATELY UNSEEDED AT BIRTH. `jobs` is empty, and the gate treats fewer
than 5 jobs as VACUOUS INPUT and exits 1. That is not an oversight: an
empty baseline makes every comparison vacuous while the gate prints a
clean line, which is the exact failure this repo keeps finding. The floor
makes it impossible to merge the gate without the harvest that gives it
something to check.
refreshed_from: PROFILER_BASELINE_V1 annotations on Console CI runs, check-runs annotations API
